notes: Building and Industrial News, vol. 11 part 2 (Internet Archive buildingindustri11211cont), the 26 weekly issues from 4 July to 26 December 1911, all Tuesdays. Same method as the later volumes of this source: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll year fits, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before the work. The issues were dated from their covers. In 1911 the paper printed the street first and the side after it ('Valley S 255 E Castro', 'Octavia and Union SW', 'Andover No. 754'), not the side first as from 1912; place.py turns the heading round when BEN_STREET_FIRST=1 is set, and without it no row is placed. extract.py ran with BEN_LOOSE=1; 30 item numbers the OCR misread were corrected from the page image. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; a cost or name not legible on the image was left out, and a cost past a column break was taken from the OCR text only where the instalments add up to the total. Owners who are private individuals are never recorded, nor is a contractor or architect who is the owner, shares the owner's surname, or is listed at the owner's premises; sureties are cut. Held back at the image (58 of 209): minor work such as signs, small repairs and shop fittings (20), storey counts that contradict the roll (15), contracts the page already carries in full from the San Francisco Call (7), unit or use counts that contradict the roll (5), small alterations and plain single houses on parcels with no page (8, held for a page), two rows on a parcel whose page credits another architect, and one street number that could not be read. 27 rows on pages that already carry a Call entry of the same weeks (the 1906-1913 newspaper recovery) were trimmed to what this paper adds (the architect, the contractor, the kind of building or the price). At 447 31st Avenue the price read here is $2,425 (three instalments of $600 and one of $625) against $2,423 in the Call entry, which is left alone. A trade contract or an alteration does not set a building's builder. The contract of 8 August at Washington and Leavenworth prints the architects as 'Chas. M. A. and Arthur F. Rousseau'; the stray initial is dropped. The contract of 19 December at Bush and Leavenworth prints Wm. Helbing, better known as a builder, on the architect's line, and he is recorded as printed. Two held facts of the later run (an electric sign of 1917 on O'Farrell Street and a porch extension of 1917 on 14th Avenue) sit on parcels seeded here and stay held as minor work.

coverage.remaining: All eight half-year volumes on the Internet Archive are read. In this volume: 139 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; they still need the image check), and 8 more were held for a page at the image. 1,115 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today. The rest have a nearest parcel that was not accepted.
